content_metadata.description: An educational video where the speaker presents the various parts of the intestine using an anatomical model. The video is focused on identifying and naming different sections of the intestine, with no narrative storyline.

qAndA.answer: The first part of the small intestine connected to the stomach is the duodenum.
qAndA.question: What is the name of the first part of the small intestine that is connected to the stomach?

qAndA.answer: The sphincter that separates the small intestine from the large intestine is the Ileocecal sphincter or valve.
qAndA.question: What is the name of the sphincter that separates the small intestine from the large intestine?

qAndA.answer: The three parts of the small intestine are the duodenum, jejunum and ileum.
qAndA.question: What are the three parts of the small intestine?

qAndA.answer: The yellow layer that would normally cover the whole area of the model is the Greater Omentum.
qAndA.question: What is the yellow layer that normally covers the whole area of the model?

qAndA.answer: The two flexures of the colon are the hepatic flexure and the splenic flexure.
qAndA.question: What are the two flexures of the colon?

text_to_speech: now let's take a look at the intestine this is the right side this is the left side first thing we notice is the greater omentum which would normally cover the whole area this area of small intestine is the jejunum ilium ilio ileocecal sphincter ascending colon here would be the liver hepatic flexure transverse colon the spleen would be here splenic flexure descending colon if we turn it around from the descending colon we have the sigmoid colon on the ascending side we have the cecum and the appendix covering this area is mesentery up here we have the duodenum the pancreas the hepatic portal vein common bile duct hepatic artery you can see the pancreas from the side as well
